content.title: Italy fail to qualify for World Cup 2026 after loss to Bosnia on penalties: Live updates and reaction from European play-off finals
content.text: Turkey, Sweden and Czech Republic qualified alongside Bosnia, but Italy will be absent for the third straight World CupBosnia celebrates qualifying for the World Cup for just the second time Getty ImagesItaly fail to qualify for third-straight World CupItaly have failed to qualify for the World Cup for the third time in a row.The four-time winners, who were reduced to 10 men after Alessandro Bastoni's 41st-minute red card, were beaten 4-1 on penalties by Bosnia and Herzegovina in Zenica.Czech Republic won their second penalty shootout in six days, this one against Denmark, to book their 2026 World Cup place while Sweden and Turkey were victorious in normal time against Poland and Kosovo respectively.Results:Bosnia and Herzegovina 1-1 Italy (Tabakovic; Kean) – Bosnia and Herzegovina won 4-1 on penaltiesCzech Republic 2-2 Denmark (Sulc, Krejci; Andersen, Hogh) – Czech Republic won 3-1 on penaltiesKosovo 0-1 Turkey (Akturkoglu)Sweden 3-2 Poland (Elanga, Lagerbielke, Gyokeres; Zalewski, Swiderski)Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDR Congo book 2026 World Cup place after Jamaica win Getty ImagesAll over in Guadalajara. DR Congo have done it, ending a 52-year wait for a World Cup place thanks to Axel Tuanzebe's scrappy, close-range finish in extra time.This was not a great match, nor the DR Congo's best performance. That won't matter to them at all.The celebrations have begun here, and back home. They won't be wrapping up any time soon.Sweden saved by Nations League Sweden are quite fortunate to have qualified for this summer's World Cup, it must be said. In the main stage of European qualifying, they finished in last place in their group, with just two points from six games against Switzerland, Kosovo and Slovenia.Kosovo, who were eliminated from qualifying today, beat the Swedes twice. Sweden, however, still progressed to the play-off round by virtue of winning their group in League C of the 2024-25 UEFA Nations League, a competition introduced to replace international friendlies only in the past decade. They won that Nations League group by finishing above Slovakia, Estonia and Azerbaijan. A trip down memory lane Let’s indulge in some nostalgia for a moment with the news that Czech Republic have qualified for the World Cup for the first time since 2006.That was an all-timer of a squad featuring the likes of Pavel Nedved, Tomas Rosicky, Milan Baros and Petr Cech, among others.Although, they were eliminated in the group stage — the Czechs finished third behind Italy and Ghana, but above the United States.Infantino's countrymen miss out again A tough night for Gianni Infantino who will not be able to watch his country at a third-straight World Cup.And no, it is not because of the ridiculously high ticket prices.The Italian has been president of FIFA since 2016 and his countrymen have not played in any of the three World Cups since.Coincidence?Gattuso apologises after Italian failure Getty ImagesGennaro Gattuso is the latest Italy manager to preside over a failed World Cup qualification bid and he came out in apology after watching his side lose on penalties in Zenica.💬 “The lads didn’t deserve to take a beating like that. We struggled, we had chances to score, but that’s football. I’m proud of my lads.“We needed this (World Cup qualification) – for ourselves, for Italy, for our sport. A blow like this is hard to take.“I’ve been in football for a few years now; sometimes I’ve celebrated, sometimes I’ve taken blows like today’s. Personally, I apologise for not making it to the World Cup, but the lads have impressed me.“My future? It’s not important right now. We’ll take this performance, but it hurts, it’s a shame.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMore extra time as DR Congo vs Jamaica finishes goalless Getty ImagesWe're heading for extra time in Guadalajara. It has been a tight, nervy game, as you might expect.DR Congo have shaded the play and certainly had the better chances but Jamaica are sticking in there. You sense it's going to take a moment of magic from someone to win this.A World Cup place beckons for whoever can produce it.As for the World Cup teams in friendly action tonight Away from the European play-offs, it was a busy night for lots of the teams that had already qualified for the World Cup.Friendlies were being played around the world and here is how a selection of them finished.Australia 5-1 CuracaoIran 5-0 Costa RicaNorway 0-0 SwitzerlandSerbia 2-1 Saudi ArabiaHaiti 1-1 IcelandSouth Africa 1-2 PanamaMorocco 2-1 ParaguayAlgeria 0-0 UruguayIvory Coast 1-0 ScotlandAustria 1-0 South KoreaEngland 0-1 JapanNetherlands 1-1 EcuadorSenegal 3-1 GambiaSpain 0-0 EgyptCzechs into Group A Czech Republic are heading for the finals and will not have to wait long to get their tournament going.They will play South Korea in Guadalajara on June 11, the opening day of the World Cup.They are the only European team in Group A and will play South Africa in Atlanta in June 18 and co-hosts Mexico in Mexico City on June 24.Tough route for Sweden in the summer Getty ImagesSweden will celebrate tonight but they face what looks like a tough group in the finals.They are are in Group F and will open their campaign against Tunisia in Guadalupe, Mexico, on June 14.Then come games against the Netherlands in Houston on June 20 and Japan in Arlington, Texas, on June 25.The walking wounded Getty ImagesHere’s how Edin Dzeko left the field after that late shoulder injury.He will be hoping for a speedy recovery in time for the World Cup.A hero in a Bosnia shirt.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUSMNT and World Cup peers in friendly action tonight Getty ImagesAnd there are a few more friendlies to come this evening that will close out this final international break before the 2026 World Cup.'We have live coverage of the USMNT's game against Portugal in Atlanta, which you can join here. Here are some others that you might want to keep an eye on:Argentina vs ZambiaCanada vs TunisiaBrazil vs CroatiaMexico vs BelgiumWho do Bosnia face in the finals? Getty ImagesHaving squeezed through to the World Cup on penalties, Bosnia will now fancy their chances of mounting a serious challenge to make the knockout stages.They will slot into Group B in the finals alongside co-hosts Canada, Qatar and Switzerland - not easy opponents but not teams who will strike fear into their hearts.They will open their tournament against Canada in Toronto on the second day of the finals, June 12, then travel to Los Angeles to face Switzerland before wrapping up their group schedule against Qatar in Seattle.More World Cup disappointment for Italy Getty ImagesThe agony. Italy gave their all and got nothing.This was an epic night in Zenica. When Kean gave Italy the lead, it felt as if it might be different this time. But no. Italy became the first former winner to fail to qualify for three consecutive World Cups.Unlike the other play-offs in 2017 and 2022, the fact that Italy got in front and had the chance to play with a little less tension gave the 500 travelling fans at the Bilino Polje hope. Bastoni’s red card at the end of the first half changed that.Italy still had chances to double their lead with a man down. They didn’t take them. Kean missed a one-on-one and Pio Esposito curled over. When Bosnia equalised, Italy could have crumbled. Instead, they stood firm. They kept going. Donnarumma kept them in it.He felt Bosnia should have been reduced to 10 men. He could not, in the end, be their saviour in a shootout. Pio Esposito took huge responsibility in stepping up for Italy’s first penalty. He blew it over the bar.Esposito is Italy’s future. But their present is not going to another World Cup.Midway through the second period in Guadalajara and there has been a bit of a shift in momentum. Jamaica, listless before the break, have started to come into it, throwing men forward with more regularity and looking dangerous. DR Congo have just brought midfielder Edo Kayembe on for winger Nathanael Mbuku — a sign, perhaps, that the nerves are starting to jangle?Bosnia's American hero Getty ImagesAvid fans of the USMNT might recognise the name of the man who scored Bosnia's winning penalty tonight.Esmir Bajraktarevic is the player who got the party started in Zenica having made the decision to represent the birthplace of his parents back in 2024.He played for the USMNT's under-19 and under-23 sides — and then made his senior debut in January 2024 —but requested to change his sports citizenship a few months later, and had it approved by FIFA.Bajraktarevic will now have the chance to play at a World Cup in the country of his birth.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDonnarumma's disappointment Getty ImagesBeing a goalkeeper in a shootout always seems to me to be better than a penalty taker. Nobody expects a goalkeeper to save a shot in those circumstances but if you do, you are a hero. Donnarumma has done that on many occasions for Italy but this time could not get near four excellent penalties. He was very agitated as he was dragged off the pitch by staff — and after making a number of big saves to keep his team in it you can maybe see why. Getty ImagesSaying that, while we are talking about passionate fanbases... intense is probably the word for the Bosnian fans! Getty ImagesEd rightly asks how Bastoni must feel but never mind them, what about the Azzurri fans back in Italy?They are one of football’s most passionate fanbases and will be hurting all over again. It’ll be 16 years and counting since they last qualified by the time the next World Cup rolls around... Getty ImagesThe photos of Bosnia's celebrations are just brilliant. Pure joy. How must Bastoni feel? Getty ImagesThe game felt like it was lost for Italy the moment Alessandro Bastoni went flying into a sliding challenge in the 41st minute.That rush of blood to the Italian's head led to a red card, given Amar Memic had raced clean through on goal on the left-hand side, and gave his team-mates a huge task to hang on to their single-goal lead.For much of the second half the Bosnians looked incapable of breaking down the resolute Italian backline until Amar Dedic whipped a brilliant cross into the penalty area, and then it was anyone's game in the shootout.A dreadful moment for Bastoni, one of Italy's best players, and one that he will feel has cost his nation a place at the 2026 World Cup.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementSelf-inflicted failure for Italy Getty ImagesThis is the third World Cup finals in a row that Italy will miss. It is becoming familiar.But one of the traditional powerhouses of the World Game, the four-time winners, failing to qualify is still a major story.In truth, they only had themselves to blame tonight. They had a couple of big chances at 1-0 to put the game to bed but missed them.Then the defending, both from Bastoni and his fellow defenders, that led to the red card was very poor.With 10 men they had a couple of decent spells but generally did not find a way to trouble Bosnia.USMNT to face Turkey in World CupWith the final four European qualification places now determined, four of the groups at this summer's World Cup are now complete.Group A: Mexico, South Africa, South Korea, Czech RepublicGroup B: Canada, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Qatar, SwitzerlandGroup D: United States, Paraguay, Australia, TurkeyGroup F: Netherlands, Japan, Sweden, TunisiaCheck out Henry Bushnell's analysis of what Turkey's qualification means for the USMNT at the link below. Photo of the night? Getty ImagesBosnians certainly like their pyrotechnics, if tonight was anything to go by. There was no shortage of flares, fireworks and a brilliant atmosphere during the match to will their team to victory.It worked.Bosnia shaded the mental battle Getty ImagesThey stayed strong all night and when Italy blinked — in the form of Bastoni’s mistimed tackle and red card — Bosnia threw everything at scoring. Maybe this photo from after their goal shows something about their steel tonight.Another chance for Bosnia to shine Getty ImagesThis summer’s World Cup will be the second time Bosnia has gone to the world’s biggest football tournament since they gained independence.The last time was in Brazil in 2014, so this has been a long time coming.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDid the fireworks have an impact?In modern football, so much research has been done to enable players to regulate themselves and be composed when it comes to taking a high stakes penalty in a shootout.Which makes me wonder — did the raft of fireworks set off somewhere in the vicinity of the stadium just as the teams set up for the shootout have an impact on the Italian players?It was audible from tv coverage and must have been loud in the stadium. You can’t prepare for everything.Goalless between DR Congo and Jamaica Getty ImagesThe European play-offs are over, but there are two inter-confederation play-offs this evening that will decide the last two places at the 2026 World Cup.The first of them — between DR Congo and Jamaica — has just reached half-time and it is goalless at the break in sun-soaked Guadalajara.DR Congo have been the better side by a decent margin so far, putting together some tidy passing moves and generally looking more technically proficient than Jamaica. They could do with creating some better chances in the second half, though, and a late pot shot from Leon Bailey was a timely reminder that games like this are not won on the balance of play.A spot in Group K with Portugal, Colombia and Uzbekistan beckons for whoever comes out on top, remember.Bosnia's standout players ASSOCIATED PRESSIt seems fitting that Esmir Bajraktarevic scored the winning penalty in a shootout where Kerim Alajbegovic also scored.Both players really stood out tonight and deserve the chance to show off their talents at the World Cup this summer. As does elder statesman Edin Dzeko, who ran the Italian defence ragged.Another national inquest awaits in Italy ASSOCIATED PRESSItaly missing out on the 2018 World Cup was a huge shock.Italy then missing out on the 2022 World Cup was beyond disappointing.Italy now missing out on the 2026 World Cup — considering it has been expanded to 48 teams — is nothing short of a national disgrace.Only Brazil have won football's biggest prize more than the Italians, but they will go without representation on the biggest stage once again.I’d say that there are no words to describe Italy’s World Cup drought, but plenty will be said about the continued Azzurri’s demise.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement James Horncastle/The AthleticBosnia unfurl their US visa.Imagine scoring a winning penalty to take your country to the World Cup. That's what Esmir Bajraktarevic just did.A chastening statistic Getty ImagesItaly are the first former champions to ever miss three World Cups in a row.Czech Republic book their 2026 World Cup place!Czech Republic are World Cup bound for the first time since 2006 after Denmark missed three of their four penalties in the shootout.The victory has spurred a party in Prague having got the better of a Denmark side who were expected to beat them.Bosnia worthy winners ASSOCIATED PRESSIt's a great story as Bosnia reach just their second World Cup finals since becoming an independent nation.And only the most churlish could deny that they deserved to get there on the night.They made the most of their minority share of possession when Italy had 11 players than piled on the pressure when their visitors were reduced to 10.It looked like they might come up short, but they kept their composure superbly in the shoot out. You've got to love football for scenes like this.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMore than 20% of the people in the world were not alive when Italy last played at the World Cup.Tears from the Italians ASSOCIATED PRESSThere are quite a few Italian players with tears in their eyes as they leave the pitch but it is all smiles for those wearing the blue of Bosnia. Dzeko is in the crowd and hugging supporters, which makes for a lovely scene. It is disbelief for Italy who miss out on a third successive World Cup. Wild scenes in Bosnia Getty ImagesThe camera is shaking, a patched up Dzeko is making peace with a riled-up Donnarumma and Bosnia are through to their first World Cup since 2014.A perfectly executed penalty shootout that Donnarumma could do little about with every kick scored.GOAL: BOSNIA WIN AND GO TO THE WORLD CUP ASSOCIATED PRESSCarnage in Bosnia! Bajraktarevic scores and Italy will not go to the World Cup. Bosnia advance!Bosnia Herzegovina: 4 ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅Italy: 1 ❌ ✅ ❌ -
